hyperedges.label: Not leaking what you cannot see

nodes.label: Build flags for one binary.      The agent gets its published arch stamped in: G
nodes.norm_label: build flags for one binary.      the agent gets its published arch stamped in: g

nodes.label: Report whether a release signing key is reachable.
nodes.norm_label: report whether a release signing key is reachable.

nodes.label: Write a .minisig beside each path using the release signing key.      Agents ref
nodes.norm_label: write a .minisig beside each path using the release signing key.      agents ref

nodes.label: Build server binaries into dist_dir, appending their checksums.      The server
nodes.norm_label: build server binaries into dist_dir, appending their checksums.      the server

nodes.label: Build the agents the server embeds, signing them so hosts can verify.      The s
nodes.norm_label: build the agents the server embeds, signing them so hosts can verify.      the s

nodes.label: An armv6 build must know it is armv6: GOARM is not readable at runtime,     so w
nodes.norm_label: an armv6 build must know it is armv6: goarm is not readable at runtime,     so w

nodes.label: LAN-only, no external backend
nodes.rationale: Reeve ships no hosted backend, no telemetry and no external account. Nothing leaves the LAN, which is the premise the whole trust model rests on: no TLS of its own, open sign-up by default, and an agent that only dials outbound.

nodes.label: One Go binary serves UI and API
nodes.rationale: The React UI is built and embedded into the server binary, so the SPA, the REST API, the installer and the agent binaries all come off one port. No separate frontend container and no dev server to run in production.
nodes.norm_label: one go binary serves ui and api

nodes.label: Catalog of services
nodes.rationale: Every service the team runs, with owner, host, address and tags, discovered from systemd, Docker and cron or added by hand.

nodes.label: Push monitoring
nodes.rationale: Per-host CPU, memory, disk, network, load, temperature and GPU plus service/container state, cron results and log errors.

nodes.label: Host and service controls
nodes.rationale: Restart or shut down a host and start/stop/restart its units or containers without a terminal. A fixed action list, admin-only, every command recording who asked.

nodes.label: Per-host credentials
nodes.rationale: Host secrets encrypted at rest, revealed only to granted people and groups, every reveal audited.

nodes.label: Public portal front door
nodes.rationale: Anonymous view of tools marked public; everything else is behind sign-in with per-user and per-group visibility.

nodes.label: Light-only theme
nodes.rationale: White content, faint grey chrome, near-black text. There is no dark theme and no toggle, because one theme means one thing to keep correct.

nodes.label: Two colors do two jobs
nodes.rationale: Blue (--link) carries every interactive state; acid-lime (--accent) is the brand only. The accent measures 1.2:1 on white, so it is never text, border, chart line or status.

nodes.label: Every column has a name
nodes.rationale: A list of records is a table with a header row. A bar, pill or button in a row must be readable without guessing what it measures.

nodes.label: Say what the state means
nodes.rationale: The UI names a state the way an operator reads it, not the way the server stores it. 'unreachable' is not 'down': the service may still run on a host that stopped reporting. 'unknown' becomes 'not monitored'.

nodes.label: Structure over shadow
nodes.rationale: Hierarchy comes from hairline borders, a rule under each page title and a small surface ladder. A shadow belongs only on something that floats over the page.

nodes.label: Four-radius vocabulary
nodes.rationale: 4px button/input/badge, 8px card/panel/table, 12px large tile, 9999px pill/avatar. No fifth radius.

nodes.label: Enter confirms every form
nodes.rationale: Every form, section and modal with editable fields submits its one primary action on Enter, done with a real <Form> and a type=submit button rather than key handlers. Button defaults to type=button so a secondary action stays inert.

nodes.label: Colorblind-validated chart palette
nodes.rationale: Series colors are assigned in order, never by rank, alternating dark and light steps so neighbouring series stay apart. The palette passes a lightness band, a chroma floor, deutan and tritan separation, and 3:1 contrast on white.

nodes.label: Tabular numerals in columns
nodes.rationale: Digits line up down a table so an operator can scan a column.

nodes.label: Session cookie auth
nodes.rationale: reeve_session resolves to that user's principal and is never elevated.

nodes.label: Host enrollment token
nodes.rationale: The agent authenticates with a Bearer rva_ token scoped to POST /api/ingest only, separate from any user session.

nodes.label: Single error envelope
nodes.rationale: Every error is {code, message} with a stable machine code, so a caller branches on the code and shows the message.

nodes.label: 404 instead of 403 for invisible records
nodes.rationale: A caller who may not see a tool or collection gets 404, not 403, so the route cannot be used to enumerate the catalog or leak restricted names.

nodes.label: Public/restricted visibility model
nodes.rationale: public means anonymous-visible on the LAN; restricted means named users and groups. A collection's visibility gates the collection, never the services inside it, so a public service cannot be hidden by filing it under a restricted collection.

nodes.label: Stable slug and /go redirect
nodes.rationale: A supplied slug is taken literally and a collision is 409 slug_taken rather than a silent rename, because it is a URL the caller is about to share. A PATCH that omits slug leaves it alone, so renaming a tool never moves a bookmark.

nodes.label: Follow-the-host endpoint resolution
nodes.rationale: A tool with no address and no url resolves through its host's last reported address, so a link survives a DHCP lease change. An offline host still redirects to the last address it reported: a stale answer beats no answer.

nodes.label: Collections replace free-text category
nodes.rationale: A named, owned, avatared set of services with its own editor and visibility grants; collection_ids replaces the whole membership set.

nodes.label: Agent update state machine
nodes.rationale: up_to_date/outdated/updating/stalled/disabled/unknown, judged on the sha256 of the running binary rather than a version string, because two builds of one version are different binaries.

nodes.label: A stalled host pauses the whole rollout
nodes.rationale: paused is true whenever stalled is non-empty. A host that can no longer update releases its slot instead of holding one, so the banner can never name a host the page renders as fine.
nodes.norm_label: a stalled host pauses the whole rollout

nodes.label: Forced update sits outside the rollout
nodes.rationale: update-now bypasses the concurrency cap and a paused rollout. The slot is recorded as forced so pressing it on a host that never comes back cannot halt the fleet.
nodes.norm_label: forced update sits outside the rollout

nodes.label: Fixed action allowlist, no shell
nodes.rationale: Actions map server-side to an argv and are never passed to a shell. The server refuses a target the host has not itself reported; there is no run-any-command action by design.

nodes.label: Commands ride the push ack
nodes.rationale: The agent is push-only and the server never dials it, so a command is collected on the next push (~15s) and answered on the one after. reboot and poweroff are acked just before they run, since they kill the agent that would report them.

nodes.label: Ingest push contract
nodes.rationale: POST /api/ingest carries contracts.Push and replies with a PushAck carrying check_now. An empty ip_address leaves the stored one alone: a tick that could not work the address out is not evidence the host moved.

nodes.label: No protocol version to negotiate
nodes.rationale: Reeve is pre-release with no agent in the world older than the server, so a payload shape change is a plain edit on both sides in one commit.

nodes.label: Credentials encrypted before they touch disk
nodes.rationale: AES-256-GCM, a random 96-bit nonce per secret, key from REEVE_MASTER_KEY. A stolen database alone reveals no secret; a stolen database plus the key reveals all of them, so the two backups are kept apart.
nodes.norm_label: credentials encrypted before they touch disk

nodes.label: Everything but secrets is plaintext
nodes.rationale: Tool names, endpoints, locations, inventories and metrics stay readable because they must be searchable, sortable and aggregatable. Treat the database as a full map of what the team runs.

nodes.label: Master-key custody
nodes.rationale: The key is never written to the database or the repo and the server refuses to start without it. There is no rotation yet: changing it makes existing ciphertext unreadable.

nodes.label: Every reveal is audited
nodes.rationale: Who, which credential, which host it opens, when, and the source IP. Grants and revocations are recorded too.

nodes.label: REEVE_TRUST_PROXY is opt-in
nodes.rationale: X-Forwarded-For is whatever the caller typed unless a proxy overwrites it, so the throttle and the reveal audit only believe it when explicitly told to.

nodes.label: Writes must come from this origin
nodes.rationale: A state-changing request carrying a session cookie needs a matching Origin. Token-authenticated callers such as the agent's push are unaffected, since they carry no ambient credential a browser would attach.
nodes.norm_label: writes must come from this origin

nodes.label: Signed agent releases
nodes.rationale: Ed25519 in minisign format, verified against a public key compiled into the agent before the downloaded bytes are written to disk. A build with no key embedded disables self-update rather than falling back to unsigned.

nodes.label: Updates only move forward
nodes.rationale: A signature proves who built a binary, not that it is the newest. The signed trusted comment carries the version, so replaying a genuine old release cannot walk a host back onto public bugs.

nodes.label: Login throttle that cannot be held shut
nodes.rationale: Five failures in fifteen minutes locks a key per IP and per account. The deadline does not extend on further attempts, so the lockout cannot be weaponised to keep someone out.
nodes.norm_label: login throttle that cannot be held shut

nodes.label: Password change signs out everywhere
nodes.rationale: Any password change, by the user, an admin, a reset link or the CLI, drops that account's sessions.

nodes.label: The host's local veto is absolute
nodes.rationale: REEVE_AUTO_UPDATE=false and REEVE_ALLOW_CONTROL=false are deliberate trust boundaries for a root process on someone else's machine. No server-side policy reaches them, because the agent ignores the ack.
nodes.norm_label: the host's local veto is absolute

nodes.label: The agent runs as root
nodes.rationale: Reading systemd, Docker, cron and journald requires it. Its unit pins PATH and unsent pushes buffer under /var/lib/reeve-agent rather than /tmp, where a local user could pre-create the path and steer what a root process writes and replays.

nodes.label: The agent distrusts its own server
nodes.rationale: It independently refuses any command target outside [A-Za-z0-9_.@:-]{1,128}, so a compromised server cannot widen the action list.
nodes.norm_label: the agent distrusts its own server

nodes.label: Single-tenant, admin sees everything
nodes.rationale: Any admin can see every host, service and audit record, and can reveal every secret. Visibility rules cover tools and secrets, not the infrastructure those run on.

nodes.label: Audit tables are append-only by convention
nodes.rationale: Not cryptographically chained. A known limit, not a guarantee.
nodes.norm_label: audit tables are append-only by convention
nodes.community_name: Audit tables are append-only by convention

nodes.label: DCO sign-off, no CLA
nodes.rationale: AGPL-3.0-or-later, copyright stays with the contributor, and the Signed-off-by trailer is what records the right to contribute the code.

nodes.label: Two-second pre-commit gate
nodes.rationale: gofmt, go vet and go test across server, agent and contracts, plus web typecheck and lint when web files are staged. It must stay under two seconds, so anything slower belongs in CI rather than the hook.

nodes.label: agent/ must not import server/
nodes.rationale: The agent runs as root on other people's machines, so its dependency surface stays as small as it is today.

nodes.label: Tests ship in the same commit
nodes.rationale: A bug fix includes the test that would have caught it.
nodes.norm_label: tests ship in the same commit

nodes.label: Frontend changes are reviewed in a browser
nodes.rationale: A passing typecheck is not evidence the UI looks right. Screenshot the views you touched and the ones you did not.
nodes.norm_label: frontend changes are reviewed in a browser

nodes.label: develop integrates, main is production
nodes.rationale: Feature branches off develop; main takes reviewed pull requests from develop only.

nodes.label: Host networking for mDNS
nodes.rationale: The server resolves .local names by sending the mDNS query itself, because no DNS server and no static Go binary can answer multicast. Multicast out of a bridge network stops at the bridge, so the container runs on the host network.

nodes.label: Build from the checkout, no registry
nodes.rationale: The Dockerfile installs web deps, builds the UI, embeds the agent binaries and compiles the server, so the only prerequisite is Docker. No Go, Node or Python toolchain and no registry login.
nodes.norm_label: build from the checkout, no registry

nodes.label: Docker NAT sits in front of ufw
nodes.rationale: A published container port is reached through Docker's own NAT rules, which ignore ufw. On the host network the server listens directly, so host firewall rules do gate it.
nodes.norm_label: docker nat sits in front of ufw

nodes.label: server users CLI
nodes.rationale: Administers accounts without the web UI, needs no master key, and works while the server is running. It refuses anything that would leave the instance unadministerable.

nodes.label: Backup carries ciphertext, not the key
nodes.rationale: Credential ciphertext travels inside the database backup and the master key does not, so the key must be stored separately or the backup is unreadable.
nodes.norm_label: backup carries ciphertext, not the key

nodes.label: SSH push install
nodes.rationale: The server confirms the host key fingerprint before sending any credential, mints a fresh enrollment token per push, and by default keeps the proven login as a credential so the next person does not have to hunt for it. A failed install stores nothing.

nodes.label: curl | sudo bash installer
nodes.rationale: Installs a root systemd unit with systemd/cron/journald/docker visibility; re-running the same command upgrades in place and preserves the token.

nodes.label: Checksum decides currency, not version
nodes.rationale: The agent reports the sha256 of its own binary and the server compares it to the build it serves, the same comparison the agent's self-update makes. A rebuild at the same version still rolls out.

nodes.label: Every filesystem, fullest first
nodes.rationale: The disk about to run out is rarely the root one. Kernel and virtual mounts are dropped, snap loop devices with them, and a bind mount counts once per device. The chart and the alert threshold still track root.

nodes.label: The signing key reaches the build only
nodes.rationale: Compose passes REEVE_SIGNING_KEY as a build secret, so it never lands in the running container or the image. Empty or missing means the embedded agents go out unsigned and say so.
nodes.norm_label: the signing key reaches the build only

nodes.label: CI gate job
nodes.rationale: go vet and test, web typecheck/lint/test/build, shellcheck, the shell unit tests and the Python release tests.

nodes.label: CI Playwright e2e job
nodes.rationale: Runs the browser suite on its own runner and uploads the report on failure.

nodes.label: CI grants contents:read only
nodes.rationale: The gate only reads the checkout, so a fork's pull request gets nothing more.

nodes.label: Actions pinned by commit, not tag
nodes.rationale: A tag can be repointed at new code, and the whole agent trust model rests on the signing key that is in scope for steps in this job.
nodes.norm_label: actions pinned by commit, not tag

nodes.label: Signing key scoped to steps, not the workflow
nodes.rationale: Without it the build still succeeds, but artifacts go out unsigned and deployed agents refuse to self-update to them.
nodes.norm_label: signing key scoped to steps, not the workflow

nodes.label: Rolling edge prerelease
nodes.rationale: develop and main push a prerelease under the fixed 'edge' tag alongside a multi-arch ghcr image.

nodes.label: Tag-triggered versioned release
nodes.rationale: A v* tag builds from VERSION and publishes signed agent and server binaries plus version and latest images.

nodes.label: Binds every interface by default
nodes.rationale: On the host network a loopback bind would need REEVE_BIND set before the first up -d is useful at all, so the default is 0.0.0.0 and the firewall is the gate. REEVE_PORT is overridable so a second instance can run alongside one holding 8080.

nodes.label: Compose refuses to start without the master key
nodes.rationale: REEVE_MASTER_KEY uses the :? form so a missing key fails at compose time with the instruction, not at runtime.
nodes.norm_label: compose refuses to start without the master key

nodes.label: Pull override for a published image
nodes.rationale: Resets the build stanza and pulls ghcr.io/thehelvijs/reeve, pinned by REEVE_IMAGE.
nodes.norm_label: pull override for a published image

nodes.label: Manual screenshot sweep after any frontend change
nodes.rationale: Including areas the change did not touch. A snapshot cannot tell you the layout is good, only that it has not changed, and axe checks only what a machine can.
nodes.norm_label: manual screenshot sweep after any frontend change

nodes.label: Pixel baselines for every page
nodes.rationale: Portal views, the modal over the list and over the map, and every authed page. /admin/server has none on purpose: it renders live machine state.

nodes.label: axe against WCAG 2 A/AA
nodes.rationale: Portal, sign-in, main authed pages and an open modal.

nodes.label: e2e pins REEVE_DEV_PORT=8099
nodes.rationale: So the suite never collides with 8080, which npm run dev uses and a locally deployed Reeve may already hold.

nodes.label: Test every trigger of a modal
nodes.rationale: A modal opens from the list, the map and the graph. Stacking contexts (Leaflet, SVG, canvas) are where z-index bites, so each path is verified separately.
nodes.norm_label: test every trigger of a modal

nodes.label: Blocking theme-boot script
nodes.rationale: Loaded synchronously on purpose: it has to set data-theme before the first paint, otherwise the page flashes the wrong theme.

nodes.label: make gate / web-check / pytest before commit
nodes.rationale: go vet and test across server, agent and contracts; tsc --noEmit and eslint --max-warnings 0; the release builder and build-config tests.
nodes.norm_label: make gate / web-check / pytest before commit

nodes.label: One schema file, re-executed on open
nodes.rationale: There are no migrations, no version table and no data to migrate, so a schema change edits schema.sql in place and every statement stays idempotent.
nodes.norm_label: one schema file, re-executed on open

nodes.label: web-build and server-assets precede build
nodes.rationale: The SSH-install and download handlers fail without the staged UI, install scripts and embedded agent binaries.
